subject: converting genotypes from JoinMap to rQTL format

messages.author: 7faeb923377c3495
messages.subject: converting genotypes from JoinMap to rQTL format
parts:
Hello,

I am using a 4-four way phase-known outbred cross for QTL mapping. The
parents segregate heterogeneously such that all possible genotypic
classes are possible. My data is currently in JoinMap format. I am
trying to convert it to rQTL format.

Joinmap as the following coding scheme to represent this.
These are the possible segregation types for the cross parents:

ab x cd (fully informative)
ef x eg (3 alleles, 1 shared, both parents heterozygotes)
lm x ll (2 alleles, 1 homozygote, 1 heterozygote)
nn x np (2 alleles, 1 homozygote, 1 heterozygote, opposite parent)
hk x hk (2 alleles, both heterozygotes)

Based on my understanding, the intercross coding options for rQTL are
thus:
ac = 1
bc = 2
ad = 3
bd = 4
A = AC or AD 5
B = BC or BD 6
C = AC or BC 7
D = AD or BD 8
AC or BD = 9
AD or BC = 10
not AC = 11
not BC = 12
not AD = 13
not BD = 14

I am trying to convert my data from Joinmap to rQTL. Here is what I
have come up with:

ab x cd = recode:
ac = 1
bc = 2
ad = 3
bd = 4

lm x ll
ll = 5 AC or AD
ml = 6 BC or BD

nn x np
nn = 7 AC or BC
np = 8 AD or BD

I am fairly certain the above is correct. I am less sure about the
following:

ef x eg code as ab x cd?
ee = 1 ac
fe = 2 bc
eg = 3 ad
fg = 4 bd

hk x hk
hh 9 AC or BD or 10
hk 10 AD or BC or 9 ?
kk 9 AC or BD or 10

I think the following are for 3:1 dominant markers:
not AC = 11 AD, BC, or BD
not BC = 12 AC, AD, or BD
not AD = 13 AC, BC, or BD
not BD = 14 AC, AD, or BC

Can anyone confirm I am doing this correctly? Or have any ideas on the
the last few segregation types?

Thanks!

messages.author: 7faeb923377c3495
messages.subject: Re: converting genotypes from JoinMap to rQTL format
parts:
Ok, I think I figured it out (with the assistance of my lab
mates :-) ). 3+ heads are better than 1.

Yes, I can code the ef x eg type using 1,2,3,4 (ab x cd). Since I know
phase, I know the true history of the alleles.

I now realize I can combine the numbers, and they are not limited to
groups of different segregation types.

So, for hk x hk, the possible kids are hh, hk, kk
This translates into ac, bc or bd, ad.
hh = ac = 1
hk = ad or bc = 10
kk = bd = 4

(genotype 9 would be used if the parents are hk x kh, for example)

For dominant 3:1 type markers (e.g. AFLPs), we can use a combination
of 11,12,13 or 14, AND one of the others.
So for example, say we have a dominant marker F with alleles F and f
(F dominant to f) and our parents are Ff x Ff, we would see two types
of kids:
F_ and ff in a 3:1 ratio. This translates in to F_ = 14 (not ff, i.e.
not BD in our coding scheme) and 4 (ff = BD).

I still welcome any thoughts or insights that confirm all this.

Genetics is fun.
Thanks!
